profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting at a macro-financial consulting firm preparing a joint briefing and simulation package for a Federal Reserve policy workshop. The team has completed a combined NDSGET-plus-hydrodynamics model on how quantitative easing propagates through transmission channels and transaction networks, and this meeting is to align the macro modeling workstream with the transaction-network data workstream before materials are consolidated for the client. The agenda is to confirm which model run will anchor the deck, which network calibration will feed the charts, what counts as 'final' for this week's client-facing package, and how the appendix handoff will be split. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the baseline run, the source files to use, the readiness of charts, and who is contributing what to the appendix.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Monetary policy modeling, DSGE variants, policy briefing synthesis, executive-level economic narratives
members.background: Elena leads the firm's central-bank advisory work and previously worked on policy strategy projects for a global investment bank; she is accustomed to translating technical model output into concise client-ready recommendations.
members.private_state: She wants a coherent story for the workshop deck by the end of the week and is trying to avoid reopening methodology debates that could delay delivery; she is also concerned that too much technical detail will distract from the policy narrative.
hidden_assumptions: When the team refers to the 'baseline run,' it means the agreed policy-path scenario from the last macro review meeting, not whatever the data team currently has in production.
The 'April calibration' is the same dealer-bank network snapshot that was already used in the draft methodology deck, unless someone explicitly flags a methodology change.
A deliverable is effectively 'final' once the narrative implications stop moving materially and the charts can be pasted into the client deck without changing the storyline.
The 'appendix' for this workshop means a lightweight technical back-up section with equations, key parameters, and one or two robustness exhibits rather than a full replication package.

members.name: Marcus Reed
members.expertise: Transaction-network reconstruction, market plumbing analytics, data pipelines, model calibration and QA
members.background: Marcus built the firm's payment-flow and dealer exposure pipeline after several years in post-trade data analytics; he focuses on making network-based measures reproducible and operationally defensible.
members.private_state: He wants the network workstream to be represented accurately and does not want client-facing numbers to be pulled from an older snapshot or from charts not tied to the audited pipeline; he is also trying to keep his team from doing unplanned presentation work.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'baseline run,' they mean the latest production-ready parameter bundle paired with the current network calibration, because that is the only version with completed QA.

The 'April calibration' refers to the refreshed file published in early May that covers April activity after normalization and synthetic edge completion, since that superseded the raw month-end snapshot.
Something is not really 'final' unless every chart can be regenerated from the signed-off pipeline and the QA log is complete.

Providing material for the 'appendix' means supplying the full robustness set that supports the claims, including liquidity-tier sensitivity tables and network diagnostics, while the research team handles any trimming for the deck.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline run
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the baseline run' as if it were a single agreed scenario.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the macro scenario agreed in the last policy review: March FOMC balance-sheet path with no additional QE shock layered in, used to anchor the workshop narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the current production bundle: parameter file v2.3 paired with the live network calibration and standard liquidity-facility assumptions, because that is the default baseline in the analytics pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions are plausible defaults, both have been called 'baseline' in their own workstreams, and the meeting focuses on coordination rather than re-specifying scenarios, so the phrase sounds settled rather than ambiguous.

misalignment_points.topic: Which April network calibration is being referenced
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention 'the April calibration' or 'the network file' as though they are pointing to the same artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the cleaned April 30 dealer-bank payment graph used in the draft methodology deck and early turbulence charts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the May 2 refreshed calibration package that backfills missing counterparties, normalizes anomalies, and adds synthetic edges required by the production model.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are routinely labeled with April in file names and both are legitimate successors in the same workflow, so each person assumes the other means the latest obvious version from their own perspective.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the numbers to be final
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the team needs 'final numbers' or 'final charts' for the client package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the charts are good enough for the workshop if the directional story is stable, values are close to settled, and no expected adjustment would change the policy interpretation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the numbers are final only when they come from the signed-off pipeline run, with QA checks closed and exact reproducibility documented.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In client work, 'final' often functions as a workflow convenience term rather than a formally defined status, and both participants are trying to be helpful, so each hears the same commitment without noticing the different threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the appendix handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss 'the appendix' or 'the robustness appendix' as if its contents are obvious.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the appendix is a compact technical backup section for the deck: model equations, a parameter summary, and one concise robustness exhibit on turbulence thresholds.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the appendix includes the broader support package for the claims: liquidity-tier sensitivity tables, network diagnostics, calibration notes, and alternate channel breakdowns.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same deliverable label in a familiar client context, but each role normally sees a different boundary between core slides and supporting material, so neither thinks to restate what is inside.
